counterfactual_missing_items: She denied any family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, or similar endocrine disorders
Normal serum calcium, phosphorus, and vitamin D levels
No adrenal biopsy, pathologic confirmation, or RET genetic testing is provided
decisive_items: 24-hour urinary metanephrines >10 000 µg (normal 25–312 µg) and normetanephrines 8791 µg (normal <600 µg)
A 31-year-old woman presented with a 7-year history of episodic palpitations, profuse sweating, and severe headaches.
response.rationale: R2 captures medullary thyroid carcinoma but leaves the catecholamine-excess symptoms and massively elevated metanephrines unexplained. R3 captures pheochromocytoma but leaves the elevated calcitonin, elevated CEA, and anterior neck mass unexplained. R1 gives the correct syndrome label but its raw support does not include both the pheochromocytoma and MTC biomarker axes. C1 is the only candidate whose raw spans jointly support the composite MEN2 phenotype with MTC and pheochromocytoma.

rejected.why: Strongly supports MTC but does not explain the episodic palpitations, sweating, headaches, or >10,000 µg metanephrine elevation.
Strongly supports pheochromocytoma but does not explain the thyroid mass, elevated calcitonin, elevated CEA, or calcified thyroid nodules.
